card.summary: The SAFE Act of 2026 amends the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act of 1978 (FISA) and related laws to reauthorize certain surveillance authorities, impose tighter rules and querying restrictions on U.S. person data collected under Section 702, restrict the purchase of personal data from data brokers by intelligence and law enforcement agencies, expand transparency, and strengthen oversight mechanisms.

summary: The SAFE Act of 2026 amends the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act of 1978 and title 18 of the United States Code to reauthorize and reform surveillance authorities. It institutes new query procedures, reporting requirements, accountability standards for FBI violations, restrictions on reverse targeting, and limits on intelligence and law enforcement acquisition and purchase of personal data from data brokers.

affected_groups.effect: Must complete annual training, obtain prior approvals for sensitive queries, generate written justifications, and face escalating personnel consequences for compliance violations.

Receive enhanced privacy protections regarding intelligence queries, restrictions on warrantless access to their communications, and limits on the purchase of their personal data by law enforcement and intelligence agencies.
affected_groups.group: United States persons and persons located in the United States

affected_groups.effect: Subject to new restrictions, minimization procedures, reporting requirements, and compliance rules regarding data collection, surveillance applications, and purchases from data brokers.
affected_groups.group: Intelligence community and law enforcement agencies

affected_groups.effect: Subject to specific limitations on directives, transparency reviews, and consistent statutory privacy protections for data demands.
affected_groups.group: Electronic communication service providers and online service providers

key_provisions: Establishes mandatory audits, training requirements, prior approvals, and written justifications for certain FBI queries under Section 702.
Prohibits warrantless access to communications and information of United States persons and persons located in the United States returned in response to covered queries, with specific exceptions.
Extends Title VII of FISA until April 20, 2028.
Imposes criminal penalties for knowingly submitting false material declarations or material omissions in FISA documents or statements, or unauthorized disclosures.
Limits intelligence community acquisition and law enforcement purchase of personal data from data brokers concerning United States persons or persons in the United States.
Expands the appointment authority and access to information of amicus curiae in proceedings before the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Court.
Requires the Department of Justice Inspector General to conduct periodic audits of FISA compliance every three years.
missing_information: Specific funding levels or authorization of appropriations to implement the audit, reporting, and compliance requirements.
Exact details of classified directives or unredacted court opinions referenced in limitations on electronic communication service providers.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The SAFE Act of 2026 amends the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act of 1978 and title 18 of the United States Code to reauthorize and reform surveillance authorities. It institutes new query procedures, reporting requirements, accountability standards for FBI violations, restrictions on reverse targeting, and limits on intelligence and law enforcement acquisition and purchase of personal data from data brokers.
summary_detail.significance: The bill reforms federal foreign intelligence surveillance authorities and domestic data acquisition practices. It alters how intelligence and law enforcement agencies handle United States person data, query procedures, court accountability, and transparency.
